technical_and_design_decisions: Target Mule ESB 3.x runtime; implement AMQP support as a Mule transport built on the standard transport framework (AbstractConnector, AbstractMessageReceiver, MessageRequester API) so it integrates natively with Mule XML configuration.
Use the RabbitMQ Java client library as the underlying AMQP 0-9-1 protocol implementation.
Provide a custom XML schema (mule-amqp.xsd) with a NamespaceHandler and BeanDefinitionParsers so users get IDE autocompletion and validation for the transport configuration (U4).
Expose a single global <amqp:connector> element holding host, port, credentials, virtual host, and reconnection strategy; all endpoints reference this one reusable configuration (U6).

Implement continuous consumption as an inbound endpoint message receiver wrapping a RabbitMQ consumer; each received message is converted into a MuleEvent and routed into the flow, with configurable acknowledgment modes (U7).
Implement instant (mid-flow) consumption via the Mule MessageRequester API so a message can be pulled from a queue at any point in a flow (U8).
Implement domain lifecycle support (deploy, undeploy with cascading undeploy of all associated apps, redeploy with update of all apps) by extending Mule's deployment module / DeploymentService (U1).
Implement application property overrides by passing deployment properties to the DeploymentService at deploy time, applied over the properties packaged inside the application archive (U2).
Deliver the base project skeleton as a Maven archetype containing placeholder configuration for endpoints, connectors, and transactions, plus a sample flow (U5).
Publish the specifications for review (U3) as version-controlled documentation (Markdown files in the repository / project wiki).
Use a Maven multi-module build with JUnit and Mule functional tests (FunctionalTestCase) against a locally running (containerized) RabbitMQ broker for integration tests.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are net effort in 8-hour workdays, not elapsed calendar time.
The target runtime is Mule ESB 3.x (community) on Java 7/8; Mule 4 support is out of scope.
AMQP 0-9-1 (RabbitMQ) is in scope; AMQP 1.0 is out of scope.
The increment scope covers message consumption (U7, U8); message publishing is out of scope except for minimal producer support needed to write integration tests.
U3 requires only preparing and publishing the specification documents for review; incorporating feedback beyond one initial review pass is out of scope.

The developer has working knowledge of Mule internals and access to a RabbitMQ broker (local installation or Docker) for testing; there is no separate QA team, so developer testing is included in the estimates.
Mule's deployment module provides the necessary extension points; no changes to unrelated core runtime code are required.
Build infrastructure (source repository, CI, licenses) already exists or can be set up within the project setup activity.
Documentation is limited to a user-facing configuration reference, examples, and release notes.
The eight user stories constitute the complete scope of the software increment.
